reflection.text: Reflection after unblinding: True MoA = Actin disruptors (cytochalasin D), Predicted = Eg5 inhibitors. Incorrect, p=0.58 overconfident.
what_was_right: We captured the true phenotype strength but mis-assigned it. Well w_2992baa437 (3uM, e2), w_e741eff746 (1uM, e7), w_bdc02a8567 (10uM, e8) all showed extreme cytoskeletal texture signals: act_std z=+168.7, +139.0, +179.3 and act_glcm_contrast z=+119.3, +104.4, +138.0 across 1-10uM. This is the canonical actin-disruptor signal. Cytochalasin D caps barbed ends and severs filaments PMID 3023337 PMID 40658853, which predicts exactly this massive increase in actin intensity STD/contrast variance, not a modest shift.

Even the low dose w_3bb1a5e523 (0.1uM, e3) already showed act_glcm_contrast +30.2 / act_std +25.9 with severe nuclear shape change nuc_solidity z=-78.3. Nuclear shape is F-actin dependent PMID 37151878 PMID 38750021, and this should have been read as early actin effect, not early mitotic condensation.

Atlas did contain the right answer from the start. compare_to_reference_atlas over 2 wells (e6): Eg5 3/10, Actin disruptors 2/10, Microtubule destabilizers 2/10 - essentially tied. Over 4 wells (e9): Eg5 6/10, Actin disruptors 3/10. Actin was consistently #2 neighbour. We correctly recorded it but hypothesis update (e13) collapsed it to 0.05 and labeled it contradicted by e10/e4.

Microscopists (e4, e5) did note 'density lower vs DMSO' but their candidate lists (Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers, Aurora, Eg5) never included Actin disruptors. That anchored us, but visual field descriptions alone cannot distinguish actin-induced rounding/multinucleation from antimitotic rounding.
what_was_wrong: We interpreted dose_response rho=+1.00 for frac_mitotic_like (e10) and rho=+1.00 for tub_mean (e11) as Eg5-specific evidence. Both are non-specific. Actin disruption causes cytokinesis failure, multinucleation and rounded cells scored as 'mitotic-like' by image classifiers, and cell rounding increases tub_glcm_contrast / tub_mean secondarily due to compacted microtubule array, not tubulin polymerization. We never tested that alternative.

We over-weighted tubulin texture/intensity increase (e2 tub_glcm_contrast +140.0, e7 +138.7, e8 +185.2, e11 rho=+1.00) and under-weighted that act_std z-scores were 5-10x larger than any plausible assay noise and monotonic in effect size (25.9 at 0.1uM -> 139-168 at 1-3uM -> 179 at 10uM). The one actin dose_response we did run was act_mean rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e14) and we used its flatness to argue 'no actin effect'. act_mean is the wrong feature for capping - mean does not change while variance/contrast (act_std, act_glcm_contrast) explodes, which e2/e7/e8 already proved.

Acquisition bias: Started at 3uM and 0.1uM (e2,e3), then filled 1uM and 10uM (e7,e8). Budget was 4 wells for 8 doses (e1). We thus sampled only high/saturating phenotypes where both actin collapse and secondary mitotic-like morphology co-exist. No dose-response for act_std, act_glcm_contrast, or multinucleation; no low-dose 0.003-0.03uM to see actin texture precede mitotic index; no replication at intermediate dose to test atlas stability. e12 cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 and e15 nuc_solidity rho=+0.80 p=0.2 were non-significant but treated as supportive of antimitotic.

Confirmation after e9: NSC vote 2/4 Eg5 and k-neighbour 6/10 Eg5 vs 3/10 Actin was taken as resolved. 0.58 (e13) was justified in rationale as 'NSC atlas favors Eg5 across 4 wells, supported by rounded condensed nuclei and tubulin texture increase'. That is phenotype + atlas concordance without biochemical specificity. True Eg5 phenotype is monopolar spindle with bipolarity loss PMID 10542155 - we never measured spindle polarity, pericentrin foci, or phospho-H3 mitotic index specifically, only frac_mitotic_like surrogate.

Literature/compound lookup after submit (e17-e22) returned identity cytochalasin D CID5458428 with no curated ChEMBL mechanisms, then PubMed hits: cytochalasin D actin polymerization 2324 hits (e21) including PMID 3023337 PMID 40658853, and Eg5 monopolar spindle 5 hits (e22) including PMID 10542155. None of this was acquired before submit_conclusion (e16). Review approved (p=0.58 moderate) citing same flawed tubulin + mitotic monotonicity logic, without requesting new data, cementing error.

citations.claim: Cytochalasin D mechanism is actin polymerization inhibition via barbed-end capping, explaining extreme act_std/act_glcm_contrast
Direct microscopic/structural capping and severing of actin filaments by cytochalasin D
Small-molecule Eg5 inhibitor phenotype benchmark is mitotic spindle bipolarity failure / monopolar spindle, which we did not directly measure
F-actin perturbation alters nuclear size/shape, relevant to nuc_solidity z=-78.3 at 0.1uM

reflection.next_experiment: If re-running: 1) stain with phalloidin for F-actin filament morphology across 0.01-10uM + quantitate multinucleation/cytokinesis failure vs true metaphase arrest by pH3; 2) direct Eg5 vs actin discrimination: high-res tubulin/pericentrin for mono- vs multi-polar spindles; 3) dose-response for act_std/act_glcm_contrast and act intensity CV, not just act_mean. This is a screening artifact lesson, not a therapeutic suggestion; no clinical implications.

- Acquisition bias: Started at 3uM and 0.1uM (e2,e3), then filled 1uM and 10uM (e7,e8). Budget was 4 wells for 8 doses (e1). We thus sampled only high/saturating phenotypes where both actin collapse and secondary mitotic-like morphology co-exist. No dose-response for act_std, act_glcm_contrast, or multinucleation; no low-dose 0.003-0.03uM to see actin texture precede mitotic index; no replication at intermediate dose to test atlas stability. e12 cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 and e15 nuc_solidity rho=+0.80 p=0.2 were non-significant but treated as supportive of antimitotic.
- Confirmation after e9: NSC vote 2/4 Eg5 and k-neighbour 6/10 Eg5 vs 3/10 Actin was taken as resolved. 0.58 (e13) was justified in rationale as 'NSC atlas favors Eg5 across 4 wells, supported by rounded condensed nuclei and tubulin texture increase'. That is phenotype + atlas concordance without biochemical specificity. True Eg5 phenotype is monopolar spindle with bipolarity loss PMID 10542155 - we never measured spindle polarity, pericentrin foci, or phospho-H3 mitotic index specifically, only frac_mitotic_like surrogate.
- Literature/compound lookup after submit (e17-e22) returned identity cytochalasin D CID5458428 with no curated ChEMBL mechanisms, then PubMed hits: cytochalasin D actin polymerization 2324 hits (e21) including PMID 3023337 PMID 40658853, and Eg5 monopolar spindle 5 hits (e22) including PMID 10542155. None of this was acquired before submit_conclusion (e16). Review approved (p=0.58 moderate) citing same flawed tubulin + mitotic monotonicity logic, without requesting new data, cementing error.

Proposed next experiment: If re-running: 1) stain with phalloidin for F-actin filament morphology across 0.01-10uM + quantitate multinucleation/cytokinesis failure vs true metaphase arrest by pH3; 2) direct Eg5 vs actin discrimination: high-res tubulin/pericentrin for mono- vs multi-polar spindles; 3) dose-response for act_std/act_glcm_contrast and act intensity CV, not just act_mean. This is a screening artifact lesson, not a therapeutic suggestion; no clinical implications.
